Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:10:1.hebrew: נפל לפניו מקול הכרייה חייב ואמאי נימא כורה גרם ליה - וכורה פטור הוא, דגרמא בעלמא הוא. (ואפילו הכורה בעל הבור, איכא למיפטריה מהאי טעמא: דכיון דמשום גרמא נפל, אסתלק חיובא דבור מיניה, ורמי אפשיעותא דקול הכורה, וההוא גרמא בעלמא דפטור ע"א.) וכשאין הכורה בעל הבור עסקינן, אלא שהוא שכירו, וכגון שהיתה בור כרויה ועומדת קודם לכן; דאי האי כרייה, הוי כורה חייב, דאין שליח לדבר עבירה, דאסור לקלקל רה"ר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:10:1.english: [If] it fell forward due to the sound of the digging, he is liable. But why? Let us say [that] the digger caused it [to fall] - And the digger is exempt, for it is merely indirect causation. (And even [if] the digger is the owner of the pit, one could exempt him for this reason: that since it fell due to indirect causation, the liability of the pit is removed from him, and it falls upon the negligence of the sound of the digger, and that is merely indirect causation for which he is exempt.) And we are dealing with [a case] where the digger is not the owner of the pit, but rather is his hired worker, and for example where the pit was already dug and standing beforehand; for if this [worker] dug it, the digger would be liable, because there is no agency for a sinful act, since it is forbidden to damage the public domain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:10:2.hebrew: בעל הבור הזיקא עביד - כלומר, בתוך שלו נמצא הנזק, וכל היכא דלא אפשר לאשתלומי מכורה — דקול גרמא בעלמא הוא — משתלם מיניה דבעל הבור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:10:2.english: The owner of the pit causes the damage - That is to say, the damage is found within his [pit], and wherever it is not possible to collect from the digger — as the sound [of digging] is merely an indirect cause — [payment] is collected from the owner of the pit.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:11:1.hebrew: בעל הבור פטור - בין שהשור הניזק שוטה בין שהוא פקח, דאמר ליה בעל הבור: אי לאו תורך לא נפל, והאי דחיפה מעשה בידים הואי ולא גרמא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:11:1.english: The owner of the pit is exempt - Whether the damaged ox is senseless or whether it is sensible, for the owner of the pit says to him: "If not for your ox, it would not have fallen," and this pushing was a direct physical act and not indirect causation.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:11:2.hebrew: רבי נתן אומר בעל הבור משלם מחצה - שהרי בין שניהם המיתוהו. אפי' הוי שור הניזק פיקח, חייב, דליכא למימר אבעי לך עיוני ומיזל, דהא חבירו דחפו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:11:2.english: Rabbi Natan says: The owner of the pit pays half - For between the two of them they killed it. Even if the injured ox was sighted, [the owner of the pit] is liable, for one cannot say [to it], "You should have looked as you walked," since the other [ox] pushed it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:12:1.hebrew: הא בתם - בעל השור משלם רביע, וטעמא מפרש לקמיה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:12:1.english: This [refers] to an innocuous [ox] - The owner of the ox pays a quarter, and [the Gemara] explains the reason further on.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:12:2.hebrew: הא במועד - דמיחייב נ"ש, דכל חד משלם מחצה, ממה נפשך: אי תרוייהו כוליה הזיקא עביד, דעל ידי חד מינייהו מיית, השתא דעבדי תרוייהו משלם כל חד פלגא; אי כל חד וחד פלגא הזיקא עביד, מאי דעבד משלם, דהא מועד הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:12:2.english: That [refers] to a forewarned [ox] - Where [the owner] is liable [for] full damages, so that each one pays half, either way: if both of them did the entire damage — for through one of them [alone] it would have died — now that both of them did [it], each one pays half; [and] if each and every one did half of the damage, he pays [for] what he did, since it is a forewarned [ox].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:13:1.hebrew: אי קסבר האי כוליה הזיקא עבד - הואיל דבלאו בור נמי מיית, הוי כאילו המיתו כולו. וכן גבי בור, הואיל ובלאו מכת נגיחות השור הוי מיית, כאילו המיתו כולו; ומשום הכי מחמיר ג' חלקים על בעל הבור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:13:1.english: If he holds [that] this [one] performed all the damage - Since even without the pit [the fallen ox] would have died, it is as though [the pushing ox] killed it entirely. And similarly regarding the pit: since even without the blow of the ox's goring it would have died, [it is] as though [the pit] killed it entirely; and for this reason [Rabbi Natan] rules stringently [to impose] three parts [i.e., three-quarters] upon the owner of the pit.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:13:2.hebrew: האי משלם פלגא והאי פלגא - כיון דבעל השור נמי כוליה הזיקא עבד, ושור תם משלם חצי נזק שהוא עושה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:13:2.english: This [one] pays half, and that [one pays] half - Since the owner of the ox also did all the damage, and an innocuous ox pays half the damage that it does.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:14:1.hebrew: ואי קסבר - הואיל ושניהם עשאוה יחד, האי פלגא עבד והאי פלגא עבד, ומשום הכי שור רביע הוא דמשלם, דהא תם הוא ופלגא מאי דעבד משלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:14:1.english: And if he holds - Since both of them did it together — this one performed half and that one performed half — therefore [the owner of] the ox pays a quarter, for it is an innocuous [ox] and [its owner] pays half of what it did.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:14:2.hebrew: ובעל השור - דתם הוא לשלם רביע, ובעל הבור דמועד הוא לשלם פלגא, ואידך מפסיד ניזק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:14:2.english: And the owner of the ox - Since it is a tam [an innocuous ox], [he is] to pay a quarter, and the owner of the pit, since it is mu'ad [forewarned], [is] to pay half; and the remainder, the injured party loses.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:15:1.english: Rabbi Natan [was] Av Beit Din [head of the court] - [as stated] at the end of Tractate Horayot.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:15:2.hebrew: שותפותאי מאי אהניא לי - בלאו שותפות נמי פלגא הוא דמשלמנא, וכיון דבעל הבור נמי כוליה הזיקא עביד, משלם ג' חלקים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:15:2.english: How did my partnership help me - Even without a partnership, it is [only] half that I pay; and since the owner of the pit also caused the entire damage, he pays three parts.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:16:1.english: You killed it - I found [it] inside yours.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:16:2.hebrew: מאי דאית לי כו' - אבל רבנן בתר מעיקרא אזלי, וסברי דבעל השור כולה הזיקא עבד. הלכך, במועד בעל השור משלם כוליה, ובתם בעל השור משלם פלגא, ופלגא מפסיד. וגבי מתניתין נמי בתר כורה אזלינן, ושניהם פטורין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:16:2.english: That which I have, etc. - However, the Rabbis follow the initial [cause] and hold that the owner of the ox performed the entire damage. Therefore, in [the case of] a mu'ad [forewarned ox], the owner of the ox pays all of it, and in [the case of] a tam [innocuous ox], the owner of the ox pays half and [the injured party] loses half. And regarding our Mishnah as well, we follow the [original] digger, and both of them are exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:17:1.english: Left a stone - [This refers to] a dug pit, and another person came and placed a stone on its rim.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:17:2.hebrew: באנו למחלוקת כו' - לרבנן, בעל האבן חייב, דהוא גרם כל הנפילה, ומשום גרמא בנזקין ליכא למיפטריה, דאבן נמי היינו בור והזיקא בידים הוא, כדתניא בפ"ג (דף כח:): "הא מה דומה לזה? אבנו וסכינו כו'". ולרבי נתן, בין שניהם משלמי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:17:2.english: We have arrived at the dispute, etc. - According to the Rabbis, the owner of the stone is liable, for he caused the entire fall, and one cannot exempt him on account of [it being] indirect causation (gerama) in damages, because a stone is also [considered] a pit and its damage is [considered] direct, as it is taught in a baraita in the third chapter (28b): "Now what is similar to this? His stone and his knife, etc." And according to Rabbi Natan, both of them pay [together].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:1:1.hebrew: וזה וזה בבור - ואפילו הכי אשמועינן מתניתין דפטור, הואיל ולא מהבלא מית אלא מחבטא, וקרקע עולם דבני רה"ר הזיקתו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:1:1.english: And both this and that [are] in a pit - And even so, the Mishnah teaches us that he is exempt, since it did not die from the foul air [of the pit] but rather from the impact, and the natural ground belonging to the public damaged it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:7:1.english: Rabba said: Here, with what are we dealing - [With that] which [the baraita] teaches: [If it fell] backward, he is liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:7:2.hebrew: במתהפך דנפל על אפיה - ברישא, ומקמי דמטא לקרקעיתה, נתהפך ונפל על גביה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:7:2.english: Where [it] tumbled, where it fell on its face - At first, and before it reached the bottom [of the pit], it turned over and fell on its back.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:7:3.hebrew: דאהני ביה - הבלא שנכנס בו בתחילת נפילתו והועילה בו להמית, היא המיתתו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:7:3.english: Which were effective on it - The fumes that entered it at the beginning of its fall and were effective on it to kill [it] — they killed it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:8:1.hebrew: הכא בנזקי בור בשור - שהשור נכנס לחצר בעה"ב שלא ברשות, ולא הפקיר לא רשותו ולא בורו, ונפל לבור והבאיש את מימיו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:8:1.english: Here [we are dealing] with damage [to] the pit [caused] by the ox - For the ox entered the homeowner's courtyard without permission, and [the homeowner] declared neither his premises nor his pit ownerless, and [the ox] fell into the pit and fouled its water.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:9:1.hebrew: דרך נפילה - על פניו משמע, דרוב בהמות הנופלין בעומק על פניהם נופלים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 53a:9:1.english: Manner of falling - [This] implies forward, for most animals that fall into a depth fall forward.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 53a:11:1.hebrew: בעל השור חייב - פי' מחצה, ובעל הבור פטור לגמרי; גזירת הכתוב מונפל שמה שור או חמור — מעצמו, ולא שיפילוהו אחרים, כדפרישית פרק קמא (דף יג. ושם.):
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 53a:11:1.english: The owner of the ox is liable - Meaning, [he pays] half [damages], and the owner of the pit is completely exempt; [this is] a scriptural decree from [the verse] "and an ox or a donkey falls therein" — [meaning] on its own, and not when others push it in, as I explained in the first chapter (13a and there).

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 53a:11:2.hebrew: ובעל הבור משלם מחצה - בשוטה או מהלך בלילה קאמר, דאי בפקח ביום, הא תנינא לעיל דפטור. וכי תימא ה"מ כשנופל מעצמו, אבל הפילוהו אחרים חייב — א"כ כשנופל נמי מעצמו ליחייב, דתחילתו בפשיעה פן יפול ע"י שוורים, וסופו באונס חייב. אלא על כרחיך שור פקח נשמר יפה ומרחק כל כך מן הבור, שאין שוורים אחרים יכולין להפילו בתוכו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 53a:11:2.english: And the owner of the pit pays half - [The baraita] is speaking of a senseless [ox] or [one] walking at night, for if [it were speaking] of a sensible [ox] during the day, did we not learn earlier that [the owner of the pit] is exempt? And if you should say that this applies [only] when it falls on its own, whereas if others pushed it in he is liable — if so, when it falls on its own he should also be liable, since its beginning is through negligence — lest it fall in through [other] oxen — and its end is through unavoidable accident, [in which case] he is liable. Rather, perforce, a sensible ox guards itself well and keeps so far away from the pit that other oxen cannot push it into it.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 53a:16:1.hebrew: לעולם קסבר האי פלגא נזקא כו' אנא תוראי בבירך אשכחיתיה - וא"ת: כיון דפלגא נזקא עבד, מה סברא היא זו דמשום דאשכחיה בבור משלם יותר ממה שהזיק? והיה רוצה ר"י לפרש דה"ק: "האי פלגא הזיקא עביד" — בעלמא, כגון בשני שוורים שהזיקו; אבל הכא, בשור שדחף חבירו לבור, הבור כוליה הזיקא עבד, כדאמר: "את קטלתיה, דבבירך אשכחיתי'", ולכך "מאי דלית לי לאשתלומי מיניה משתלמנא מינך". וחזר בו ר"י מפירוש זה, דא"כ, מועד לר' נתן אמאי משלם מחצה? כי היכי דמהני שותפות לבור, שאין הבור משלם אלא חצי ממה שהזיק, כמו כן יועיל שותפות הבור לשור ולא ישלם השור מחצה! ובתם נמי איכא להקשות: אמאי משלם רביע? ע"כ נראה דבור נמי פלגא נזקא עבד, ומשום שגמר ההיזק ודומה כמי שעשאו כולו, אמרינן: כי ליכא לאשתלומי מבעל השור, משתלם מבעל הבור:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 53a:16:1.english: Actually, he maintains [that] this one [performed] half the damage, etc., "I found my ox in your pit" - And if you ask: Since [the pit] performed [only] half the damage, what reasoning is this that because he found it in the pit, [the owner of the pit] pays more than what he damaged? The Ri [Rabbi Yitzchak] wanted to explain that this is what [the Gemara] means: "This one performed half the damage" [applies] in general, such as when two oxen caused damage; but here, with an ox that pushed its fellow into a pit, the pit performed the entire damage, as [the owner of the dead ox] says, "You killed it, for I found it in your pit," and therefore, "what I cannot collect from him [the owner of the damaging ox], I collect from you." However, the Ri retracted this explanation, because if so, why does a mu'ad [forewarned ox] pay half according to Rabbi Natan? Just as the partnership [with the ox] helps the pit — so that the pit pays only half of what it damaged — so too the partnership with the pit should help the ox, and the ox should not pay half! And regarding a tam [an ordinary ox] as well, one can ask: why does it pay a quarter? Therefore, it appears that the pit also performed [only] half the damage, and because it completed the damage and is like one who did all of it, we say [that] when one cannot collect from the owner of the ox, one collects from the owner of the pit:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 53a:4:1.hebrew: שמואל לטעמיה דאמר להבלו וכ"ש לחבטו - וא"ת: דלמא כי מחייב בחבטו, היינו כשנתקל בבור; אבל הכא הכרייה גרם לו ליפול, וגם נחבט בקרקע עולם — בהא הוה פטור? וי"ל: דשפיר הוי לטעמיה, דאשכחן דמחייב בחבטה כשנחבט על ידי מעשיו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 53a:4:1.english: Shmuel [conforms] to his line of reasoning, as he says: for its fumes, and all the more so for its impact - And if you ask: Perhaps when he holds [one] liable for its impact, that is [only] when [the animal] stumbled on the pit [itself]; but here, [where] the [sound of the] digging caused it to fall, and it also struck the natural ground, in this [case] he would be exempt? And one can answer: Indeed it conforms to his line of reasoning, for we find that he holds [one] liable for impact when it is struck as a result of his actions.
